verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents API keys plus tenant tokens, which are described as short-lived, scoped credentials generated from an API key. Their embedded filters restrict which documents each search request can see, so an agent can be given a time-limited, data-scoped search credential. The evidence only shows scoping of search results, not least-privilege keys limited by action (e.g., read-only vs. write) or by index, and nothing addresses agent-specific credential workflows. Missing for 10: documented action- and index-scoped API key permissions, agent-oriented credential guidance (e.g., for the MCP server), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
